objective.architecture_invariant: retain the qualified Gummel electron/energy <-> Poisson fixed-point architecture for performance lanes; basis lane is diagnostic-only and does not alter the production architecture
objective.metric: average fixed-point loops per electron step plus discrete electron-response Jacobian identification
objective.target: O(10) or lower fixed-point loops and a directly measured 20x20 electron-response matrix with explicit finite-difference quality checks
objective.success_condition: identify a stable useful small-gamma A1 or A2 operating range while independently resolving the nonlocal electron-potential response structure; no promotion without equal-physics parity

frozen_invariants: qualified plasma equations, chemistry, RF state, wall models and BC ownership
chi_e=100, chi_h=400, dt_h/dt_e=4 for screening performance lanes
Picard-2x relaxation, nonlinear tolerances, fixed-point tolerances and stopping criteria
one-heavy-cycle/four-electron-step short discriminator horizon for screening lanes
basis lane uses the Gen12 step-1 accepted state as a read-only prior-generation operating point and changes only prescribed diagnostic potential perturbations
no result from one Gen13 lane may alter another Gen13 lane while the generation is active

hypotheses.statement: The thermal-slope screened-Poisson mechanism is useful when scaled to the trajectory-measured response magnitude, approximately gamma=0.025-0.05, rather than gamma=1.
hypotheses.mechanism: Use beta_eff=gamma*(e/eps0)*n_e/T_e[eV] only in the Poisson Gummel iteration operator. Gen12 current-state directional evidence places the effective local scale at O(0.05), so bounded small gamma should retain contraction benefit without the Gen11 over-stiff stall.
hypotheses.falsifier: Reject this bounded A1 range if both gamma=0.025 and 0.05 fail to complete four electron steps stably, fail to reduce fixed-point work materially versus the same-lane Picard-2x control, or violate same-time physical parity.
prior_evidence: Gen11 gamma=1 reduced the first step from 6 to 2 FP iterations but stalled above 3000 iterations on the next step.
Gen12 run 35975788441 found median gamma_A1≈0.0258 on step 1 and ≈0.0503 on step 2 using current-state sampling.

hypotheses.statement: The transport-ratio surrogate n_e*mu_e/D_e gives a similarly scaled but potentially better local Jacobian preconditioner than the thermal A1 surrogate when gamma is O(0.025-0.05).
hypotheses.mechanism: Use beta_eff=gamma*(e/eps0)*n_e*mu_e/D_e in the Poisson Gummel iteration operator, with mobility and diffusion transferred from the current fast-plasma state. The correction vanishes at fixed-point convergence.
hypotheses.falsifier: Reject this bounded A2 range if both gamma=0.025 and 0.05 fail stability/work/parity gates, or if A2 does not provide a reproducibly useful contraction improvement at the same frozen settings.
prior_evidence: Gen12 run 35975788441 found median gamma_A2≈0.0286 on step 1 and ≈0.0557 on step 2.
A2 tracks A1 in local scale but derives the slope from the actual transport ratio mu_e/D_e.

hypotheses.statement: The strong off-diagonal Gen12 response is a real property of the discrete electron map and can be resolved directly by basis perturbations rather than inferred from the rank-18 Gummel trajectory.
hypotheses.mechanism: Freeze the prior-generation step-1 accepted electron state, prescribe the accepted potential profile, and evaluate one electron timestep for a reference plus symmetric +/-delta_phi perturbation in each of 20 cells. Central differences produce all 20 Jacobian columns; plus/minus symmetry measures local finite-difference nonlinearity.
hypotheses.falsifier: Classify unresolved if any basis case fails, if the central-difference odd response is dominated by even/nonlinear error, or if the resulting response matrix cannot be numerically distinguished from a rank-deficient/noise-dominated matrix.
prior_evidence: Gen12 step-2 trajectory contained 514 secant pairs but only rank 18/20.
Gen12 current-state least-squares response had off-diagonal Frobenius fraction about 0.966, indicating strong nonlocal coupling.
